text:
elaine: Filing follow-up: compacting prefix assignment metadata to reduce memory churn and speed handoffs. idea: maintain a compact epoch-log per-shard instead of full prefix records for short-lived prefixes.
omar: can you sketch what goes into the epoch-log?
elaine: each entry: prefix_id, assign_epoch, assign_token (short), last_renew_ts, tombstone_flag. we keep full metadata only for hot prefixes; everything else is in epoch-log which is append-only and compacted periodically.
viktor: benefits: fewer cache line loads on handoff path and cheaper snapshoting for orchestrator. downside: extra complexity on reads that hit a compacted prefix.
clare: how do reads find the authoritative owner when metadata compacted?
elaine: plan: local worker keeps an in-memory LRU for resolved owners. miss -> consult shard-epoch-log index, which is small and can be kept in mmap. if index says owner is X and X!=local, we RPC. we avoid full object rehydrate.
omar: race concern: if assign happens fast, epoch-log may show multiple entries. need a deterministic way to pick most recent visible assign that is committed. add commit_marker per-epoch entry.
viktor: agree. also add monotonic sequence per-shard so we can do CAS-like semantics when applying a new assign. new_assign(seq_no) only accepted if seq_no > latest_seq. orchestrator increments seq.
clare: eviction correctness: if we demote based on compacted state, we might evict a prefix that's still being served by another worker. need to ensure rehydrate path tolerates that.
elain e: typo: 'elaine' : )
elaine: ha. fixed.
elaine: eviction safety: before evicting a compacted prefix, require a soft-lease probe to the purported owner. if owner responds still holding, delay eviction. this probe is cheap since owner_id is in epoch-log.
omar: probe RPCs could add load. optimize: batch probes per-shard when eviction sweep runs. also only probe if last_seen_ts < eviction_probe_threshold_ms.
viktor: another idea: keep a tiny bloom filter per-shard of recent owners to detect likely hits without RPC. if bloom says negative -> safe to evict. positive -> probe.
clare: bloom false positives cause extra probes but okay. false negatives unacceptable; choose params to minimize that.
elaine: compaction policy: keep last N entries per-prefix in epoch-log (N=2) and GC older entries after safe_window_ms (default 10s). helps with short-lived flaps.
omar: tests: race sim where assign->reassign->evict interleave with network delays. assert no lost-serve and no double-evict. also measure memory reduction for 1M small prefixes.
viktor: migration: start with dual-write: continue writing full metadata plus epoch-log. after a day of telemetry, flip read-path to prefer epoch-log for cold prefixes. fallback remains intact for safety.
clare: metrics to add: epochlog_compaction_rate, epochlog_probe_count, compacted_eviction_delay_ms, compacted_prefix_miss_rate. add alert if compacted_prefix_miss_rate spikes.
elaine: implementation steps: 1) epoch-log wire format + compact writer, 2) mmap index + fast lookup API, 3) batched probe service, 4) bloom per-shard experiment, 5) dual-write migration and canary rollout.
omar: rollout: dev -> staging -> 2% prod -> 20% -> 100% with automatic rollback trigger on any of: compacted_prefix_miss_rate > 1% OR p99_rehydrate_latency increase > 20% OR double-evict incidence > 0.
viktor: docs: add operator playbook for emergency restore path: enable full-metadata reads per-shard via admin flag.
ops-bot: note: created dashboard stub 'epoch-log-compact' and scheduled weekly retention job.
clare: thanks. i'll write RFC-followup doc with diagrams and run the sim.
elaine: thanks all. pairing: @omar on mmap index, @viktor on probe batching, @clare on tests.
